findings.title: Conditional passkeys UI is now enabled during re-authentication with a known user, breaking the re-authentication contract
findings.body: In `authenticate()`, the WebAuthn conditional-UI form data is now set up whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which includes the case where `context.getUser() != null` (re-authentication, e.g. prompt=login). Previously the code only called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in the `else` branch, i.e. only when no user was set. Enabling conditional UI (autofill passkeys on the username field) during re-authentication changes the login page into an autofill/conditional-UI page for a user who is already identified; the username is hidden and the page is expected to be a password-only re-authentication form. This is a behavioral regression for re-authentication flows and contradicts the intent of the surrounding code, which explicitly sets `USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` and the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` note for the re-authentication case. The same change in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) enables conditional UI on error pages during re-authentication. The condition should remain restricted to the non-re-authentication branch (user == null), as before.

findings.title: UsernameForm skips the username form during re-authentication when conditional passkeys are enabled, but `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is not defined in this class
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (line 47), but this method is only defined in `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160) as `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. `UsernameForm` extends `UsernamePasswordForm`, so it compiles, but the inherited implementation checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. In `UsernameForm`, `webauthnAuth` is only non-null when constructed with a `KeycloakSession` (`UsernamePasswordForm(KeycloakSession)`); the no-arg constructor used by the provider factory leaves it null, so the guard behaves inconsistently depending on construction path. More importantly, the semantic change means that during re-authentication (user already set) with passkeys enabled, `UsernameForm` no longer calls `context.success()` and instead falls through to `super.authenticate(context)`, which renders the username/password form with the username hidden — but for a split username+password flow (as configured in `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`), the subsequent `PasswordForm` step then runs with the user set, which is a different flow shape than intended. The condition should be scoped so the skip only happens when passkeys conditional UI is actually active for this authenticator instance, not merely when the realm has passkeys enabled.

findings.title: Refactored `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` changes behavior for subclasses that override it to return false
findings.body: `fillContextForm()` previously checked `if (user != null)` before building the `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` and setting `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS`; it now calls `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (line 101), whose base implementation returns `context.getUser() != null` (line 129). `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides this to return `false` (line 65-67) so that authenticators are not listed during conditional UI. However, the base `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` still sets `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED` based on a local `isUserIdentified` variable that is only set to `true` inside the `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` branch (line 108). For `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` during re-authentication (user != null), `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` returns false, so `isUserIdentified` stays false and `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED` is set to "false" even though a user is identified — the template may then render the page as an ID-less/passwordless page rather than a re-authentication page. The refactor conflates "user is identified" with "authenticators should be listed"; these are separate concerns and the `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED` flag should still be derived from `user != null`.

findings.title: Error response during conditional-UI passkey failure sets re-authentication form attributes unconditionally
findings.body: `createErrorResponse()` now calls `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (line 53). That helper only sets `USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note is "true", so in the normal (non re-authentication) conditional UI case it is a no-op. However, when a passkey conditional-UI authentication fails during re-authentication (user already set, note = "true"), this marks the form as re-authentication — which is correct — but the method is invoked on every error response, including errors that occur in the plain username/password flow where the user was NOT previously set (e.g. `WEBAUTHN_ERROR_API_GET` from the browser). In that case the note is absent and the call is harmless, but the placement suggests it is meant to run only for re-authentication errors; if the note is ever set by another path (e.g. a previous execution in the same auth session), a non re-authentication error page would incorrectly hide the username field and disable registration. The call should be guarded by an explicit check that this error occurred during a re-authentication flow, not placed unconditionally in the shared error-response path.

findings.title: Static import from `browser` package into `util` package creates a package cycle and widens visibility of an internal constant
findings.body: `AuthenticatorUtils` (in `org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.util`) now statically imports `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` (line 35), and the constant was changed from `protected` to `public` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java line 58) solely to make this import possible. This introduces a dependency from the generic `util` package back into the `browser` package (a package cycle: browser → util → browser), and exposes an internal flow-state constant as part of the public API surface of `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`. The constant is an implementation detail of the username/password form flow; making it `public` invites external use and makes future refactoring harder. The constant should remain `protected`/package-private and the note name should either be defined in `AuthenticatorUtils` itself or in a neutral location, with `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` referencing it from there.

findings.title: Test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` uses inverted assertion logic that always passes
findings.body: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the check for absence of the WebAuthn button is written as: `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button");` inside a `try` block, with `catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`. `driver.findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is absent, so the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` line is never reached in the expected (passing) case — the test passes via the catch block. If the element IS present, `findElement` returns a non-null element, `assertThat(element, nullValue())` fails with an `AssertionError`, which is also caught by the broad `catch (Exception)` and silently treated as expected. The test therefore cannot fail when the WebAuthn button is incorrectly shown; the assertion is dead code. The correct pattern (used elsewhere in the codebase) is `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))`, as done in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` before this PR. Both occurrences (lines 291-296 and 312-317) have the same defect, so the test does not actually verify that passkeys are hidden for a user without a passkey during re-authentication.

findings.title: Re-authentication test submits only a password on a form where the username field is hidden but present, relying on stale form state
findings.body: In `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, after re-authentication with `prompt=login`, the test calls `loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost"))` (line 377) — a single-argument login that submits only the password. This works only because the hidden username field retains the previously entered username from the initial login form submission in the same browser session. The test then asserts `Assert.assertEquals("Invalid password.", loginPage.getInputError())` and later expects a successful password login for `user.getId()`. This is fragile: it depends on the hidden input's value persisting across page loads and on the specific template rendering the hidden username with the attempted username. If the template changes (e.g. the hidden field is rendered empty, or the form posts to a different action), the test would submit an empty username and fail with "Invalid username or password" rather than "Invalid password", or authenticate the wrong user. The test should explicitly assert the hidden username value (e.g. `loginPage.getAttemptedUsername()` equals the expected user) before submitting, as done in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, to make the precondition explicit and the failure mode diagnosable.

findings.title: New `configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation)` call in `addTestRealms` is undefined in the shown file and may break realm setup
findings.body: `addTestRealms` now calls `configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation)` (line 73) before adding the realm, but no such method is defined in the shown file content and it is not a standard override of `AbstractAdminTest`/`AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest` visible here. If this method is inherited from a superclass it may be fine, but if it is expected to be defined locally (e.g. to set up the `test-user@localhost` user that the new tests rely on at lines 299, 323, 377, 404), its absence would cause a compile error; if it exists in a superclass it may perform additional realm mutations not obvious from this diff. The new tests depend on a pre-existing user `test-user@localhost` with a known password (`getPassword("test-user@localhost")`), which is not created by `registerDefaultUser()` (that creates `userwebauthn`). The diff does not show where this user is created; if `configureTestRealm` does not create it, tests `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` will fail at runtime with user-not-found. This dependency should be made explicit in the test file.

findings.title: Changed assertion in `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` now expects the webauthn form to be present after username submission, but does not verify it is functional for the identified user
findings.body: The test `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` was changed to assert that `//form[@id='webauth']` IS present (line 194, 200) after submitting the username, where previously it asserted the form was absent. This matches the behavioral change in `UsernamePasswordForm` (conditional UI now enabled when user is set), but the test only checks element presence via `driver.findElement(...)`. It does not verify that the conditional UI / WebAuthn form is actually wired to the identified user (e.g. that the challenge is bound to that user's credentials, or that the autofill attribute is set on the password field rather than the username field). Given that the production change enables conditional UI during a state where the user is already identified (see the high-severity finding on `UsernamePasswordForm.java:115`), this test should assert the rendered page semantics (e.g. `loginPage.getPasswordAutocomplete()` includes `webauthn`, or the hidden username value) to catch regressions where the conditional UI is attached to the wrong input. As written, it only asserts a DOM node exists, which would also pass if the form were rendered in a broken state.
